content: An insulator is a genetic boundary element that serves two distinct functions in the regulation of gene expression. It can act as an enhancer-blocking element, preventing the interaction between an enhancer and a promoter, or, less commonly, as a barrier that prevents the spread of condensed chromatin proteins into regions of active chromatin. The necessity for insulators arises in situations where two adjacent genes on a chromosome exhibit significantly different transcriptional patterns. In such cases, it is crucial to ensure that the mechanisms inducing or repressing transcription in one gene do not interfere with the transcriptional activity of the neighboring gene. Reference: Burgess-Beusse, B., et al. (2002). The insulation of genes from external enhancers and silencing chromatin. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, 99(Suppl 4): 16433–16437. DOI: 10.1073/pnas.162342499.
